question: What drives the normal-domain failure of this frozen EBM?
most_supported_interpretation: Failure to generalize to short genuine speech from new source domains. Actual EER-tail errors concentrate in short VCC recordings, whose final representations fall near T spoof support. Original duration, source domain and repeated-padding processing interact; unique acoustic cause and duration-versus-padding causality remain unresolved.
verified: 3419 original waveforms were analyzed on the server; the primary acoustic subset is all1156 DF nocodec normal waveforms. All are16kHz mono PCM16.
48 measured acoustic descriptors did not show reliable incremental prediction of normal errors beyond source+duration under5-fold source x speaker validation and7-comparison intervals.
Within-speaker/duration partial rank associations were small in magnitude; maximum absolute observed value was0.160597.
Rejected VCC2018 normals:334;29.9401% nearest T reference is genuine versus90.1198% nearest held-out DF reference is genuine. VCC2020:154;44.1558% versus96.7532%. References are balanced by class.
Existing paired10dB noise increased VCC2018 normal rejection by8.6042pp and VCC2020 by21.6401pp. Opus32k increased it by4.0153pp and6.1503pp.

Frozen normal-only reference replacement was not sufficient: source centers EER3.20%, source translation5.00%, source normal-score standardization3.60%, DF3normal prototypes12.50%, compared with native3.35%. All methods reported.
Layer-attention flattening reduced normal rejection to0% at the prior threshold but raised spoof acceptance to33.5778% and EER to7.4889%; it did not selectively repair the error.

Completed DF-internal supervised direction probes achieve EER1.6056%–1.7333%, so some class-discriminating information remains in the frozen final representation. This is not T-to-DF transfer performance.
not_established: A specific microphone, resampling algorithm, spectral band, pitch, accent or vocal-production factor as the unique physical cause.
Whether the pretrained XLS-R frontend or a particular learned backend layer originates the harmful representation shift.
Whether retraining with additional normal domains alone suffices; all new reference tests kept the EBM fixed.
Independent unseen-domain generalization; DF has been repeatedly inspected and internal DF references/probes use target-domain training folds.
Whether limited unique speech duration or the repeated-padding pattern causes the short-source failure.
Boundary-discontinuity descriptors did not provide reliable added prediction beyond source and duration; this does not prove every padding effect absent.
excluded_by_user: Silence-distribution dependence was not investigated as a cause; no silence-duration/proportion predictors were used.
family_mapping: Official public mapping retrieval unavailable within bounded attempts; source-family dependency remains unresolved.
critical_metric_scope_correction: 19LA fixed-threshold operating errors and DF own-EER tail errors are distinct. Earlier broad normal-domain findings remain valid for the fixed threshold; actual EER-tail diagnosis is recorded in EER_tail_complete.json.

limitations: Removing short normals changes the test population; it is not padding removal or a model improvement.
Native duration and wrap repetition are linked; their separate causal effects require a same-waveform input intervention.
T has short-view training as well as original recordings. Original-duration counts do not measure all effective augmented training exposure.
Only36 of1156 nocodec normal waveforms are rejected at the full-DF EER threshold; tail-model feature tests have limited power.
The EER threshold is retrospective and must not be presented as a deployment threshold.
